raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #43460
* __->__ #43459
* #43458
* #43457
* #43456
* #43455
* #43454
* #43453

## Motivation

To bind the first and last stages of a pipeline rank's stack, `make_layers` built the neighbouring layers again on the meta device and read the stages they declared. Building a layer can have effects the meta device does not stop (streams, communicators, explicit devices), its choices had to be re-derived from modules nobody runs, and every bound stage kept its neighbour's and its producer's declaration, holding their reads, updates and transforms (and so their modules) for the life of the model.

## Modifications

- **Record a neighbouring stage by the facts binding reads of it.** `facts_of()` reduces a declaration to the capabilities binding reads (`UpdateFacts`, `ReadFacts`, `TransformFacts`) without the declarations it is chained to; neighbours and recorded producers are such facts. A read's kernels are not among them: binding takes kernels only from the reads of the stages it binds, so `ReadFacts` supplies none. A rank whose first stage would have to run the output transform of an attention on the previous rank is rejected (no model declares one); a test covers it.
- **Let a model declare its neighbouring stages without building the layers.** `make_layers` / `make_pp_layers` take `stage_facts`: the model's shared declaration function, which returns the stages the layer at a global index declares, and which the layer also uses for its own declarations. Under PP each layer a rank builds is checked against it; a mismatch names the layer, the stage and each differing field with both values. Models not yet migrated stay on a transitional list that keeps the meta-device path; Nemotron-H, whose declarations already came from its pattern, gives a function and leaves the list. #43460 migrates every other model and removes the list.
- **Drop stage boundary forwarding and exports nothing uses; drop the keyword arguments no output move is given.**
- **Describe neighbouring stages, exit policies and sum completers as they are** in the layer boundary developer guide, including a table of exit policies and which of their decisions are fixed at construction.

## Accuracy Tests

How the stack is checked:
- **Unit tests**: the 39 layer-boundary test files pass at the head of every PR in the stack, apart from the two AMD-only `test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd` cases that fail on NVIDIA on main too; the test files that changed most recently pass on every commit. The full `test/registered/unit` suite (926 files, one process per file) shows no failure on the stack's head that main does not have.
- **Plan comparison**: an out-of-tree harness binds every stage plan for seven stack shapes (decoder layers with and without an output transform, MHC, Nemotron-H patterns, Kimi K3, Qwen4-exp, NemotronNAS-style attention-only layers, single-stage appends) over 23 parallel configurations, four boundary reductions and one or two pipeline ranks (3,928 scenarios), and compares each bound plan leaf by leaf with the parent commit's.
- **GPU**: dummy weights are seeded per TP rank and scaled (0.05, norms 1.0), so that a sum taken twice or a mixture of rank partials changes the output; the default dummy weights give every rank the same shard and would hide both.
- GPU results below were measured on these commits as based on main `516fd1c1b5` unless marked as on the merge candidate; rebasing onto current main had no conflicts, and the CPU checks were run again after it.
- **On the merge candidate** (head of this stack against main `961bcf481d`, H200, asymmetric dummy weights unless noted): DeepSeek-V2-Lite input-scattered PP2 is bit-identical to PP1 (main crashes on it); Nemotron-H cut between a mixer and its FFN differs from PP1 only at the rounding level of the FFN-to-mixer cuts (main: 0.93 and 2.21); Llama, Qwen3-MoE, GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V2-Lite are bit-identical to main at PP1 and PP2; GSM8K (real DeepSeek-V2-Lite weights, 250 questions, TP4 with attention DP2 and the dense FFN fully data-parallel) gives 0.360 at PP2, 0.364 at PP1 and 0.368 on main at PP1, medians of three runs whose run-to-run spread is 0.012–0.016. The last revision of the stack changed only comments, docstrings, an equivalent condition and explicitly set attributes after these runs; its bound plans are identical.

For this PR: the plan comparison differs only in how a pipeline rank's neighbour appears in a bound plan (a `ReadFacts` instead of the read object), on an edge whose read does not run on the sending rank.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No forward-path change.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

@@ -122,7 +122,7 @@ with layer_stack():
 
 Every stage binds when the stack closes, once its producer and its consumer are known: the stage appended before it and the one appended after it. The last stage ends the model's layer stack and is marked terminal, unless a later layer declares a stage. A boundary's `declaration` is usable at once; when the stack closes, it is replaced by the declaration with its place in the stack (its `previous` and `terminal`), and the plan is bound. An error raised while binding carries a note naming the `append_stages()` call it came from. A terminal stage leaves no work for a following layer, except the final-norm finalize handoff described in [Enter and leave the layer stack](#enter-and-leave-the-layer-stack). A NextN/MTP draft module is its own stack: its layer enters the stack and ends it, even when it reuses the target's decoder class.
 
-Pipeline parallelism splits one layer stack across ranks, so the first and last local stages have neighbours that another rank builds. `make_layers()` finds them without communicating: when its stack closes, it builds the layer before the rank's first local layer and the one after its last again, with the model's own layer function inside `building_neighbour_layer()` (on the meta device), reads the stages they declare and discards them. A stage's declaration depends only on the config and the global layer index, so both ranks see the same boundary. A layer that declares no stage is passed over in favour of the next one out. These neighbours are built only if the stack appended stages, and after the local layers. A neighbour is never loaded or run, so a layer constructor must run on the meta device, must skip the host and device resources only a running layer needs (tables, streams, engines, communicators) when `is_building_neighbour_layer()` is true, and must not depend on which pipeline rank builds it. The meta device alone does not stop a constructor that names a device explicitly.
+Pipeline parallelism splits one layer stack across ranks, so the first and last local stages have neighbours that another rank builds. The model gives `make_layers()` (or `make_pp_layers()`) its shared declaration function, `stage_facts`: given a global layer index, it returns the stages that layer declares, in order (an empty tuple for a layer that declares none), from the config, the layer index, construction options known before the layer is built, and the fixed parallel topology, never from built modules or provider state. The layer declares its own stages with the same function, so both ranks derive a boundary from one source; under pipeline parallelism `make_layers()` also checks each layer it builds against the function. When the stack closes, it asks the function for the stages next to it, nearest layer first, passing over a layer that declares none, and keeps only what binding reads of them (`facts_of()`: the capabilities a read, update and output transform declare, not the objects). A model that does not give the function yet is on a transitional list: its neighbours are built again with the model's own layer function inside `building_neighbour_layer()` (on the meta device), which must then skip the host and device resources only a running layer needs when `is_building_neighbour_layer()` is true and must not depend on which pipeline rank builds it. A model off that list must give the function to run under pipeline parallelism.
 
 Each item may include a third element containing constructor options: an attention stage accepts `qkv_latent_func` (for example `{"qkv_latent_func": self.self_attn.prepare_qkv_latent}`) and `fusions`; an FFN stage accepts only `fusions` (see [Fusion providers](#fusion-providers-and-output-decisions)). An option a stage does not take is rejected when appended. Pass declarations fresh from `declare_attn()` / `declare_ffn()`: one taken from a bound boundary already has its place in a stack, and is rejected.

-- The layer constructor runs on the meta device, allocates nothing when `is_building_neighbour_layer()` is true, and declares the same stages whichever pipeline rank builds it: `make_layers()` builds the layers next to a rank's own that way to read their stages.

+Each exit has its own policy, and what it decides from fixed facts (the parallel configuration, the declarations and the bound path) is decided when the plan is built and recorded on the path as `ExitFacts`; only what depends on the batch is decided for it:

+| Exit | Entry point | May decide |

+| Mixer | `finish()` | Leave its declared sum to the next stage's input (before an FFN); carry it to the next mixer's input (without attention DP); or complete it |

+"""What binding reads of a stage it does not run: the stage before or after
+a stack on another pipeline rank, and the producer a bound stage records.
+
+A stage's read, update and output transform are objects that hold the
+layer's modules and state. Binding a neighbouring stage reads only the
+capabilities they declare, so a neighbour, and the producer a stage keeps,
+is recorded as those values alone: no module, bound method or declaration
+history stays referenced once the stack is bound."""
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+
+
+class UpdateFacts(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """The capabilities a ResidualUpdate declares (see ResidualUpdate)."""
+
+    is_plain_add: bool
+    applied_at_exit: bool
+    outlives_layer: bool
+    writes_stream: bool
+    quantized_sum: bool = False
+
+    @classmethod
+    def of(cls, update) -> "UpdateFacts":
+        if isinstance(update, cls):
+            return update
+        return cls(
+            is_plain_add=update.is_plain_add,
+            applied_at_exit=update.applied_at_exit,
+            outlives_layer=update.outlives_layer,
+            writes_stream=update.writes_stream,
+            quantized_sum=update.quantized_sum,
+        )
+
+
+class ReadFacts(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """The capabilities a ResidualReadout declares (see ResidualReadout).
+    Binding takes kernels only from the reads of the stages it binds, never
+    from a stage recorded by its facts, so these supply none."""
+
+    is_plain_norm: bool
+    reads_before_dp_gather: bool
+    reads_after_attn_tp_gather: bool
+    completing_fusions = ()
+    gathering_reads = ()
+
+    @classmethod
+    def of(cls, read) -> "ReadFacts":
+        if isinstance(read, cls):
+            return read
+        return cls(
+            is_plain_norm=read.is_plain_norm,
+            reads_before_dp_gather=read.reads_before_dp_gather,
+            reads_after_attn_tp_gather=read.reads_after_attn_tp_gather,
+        )
+
+
+class TransformFacts(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """What an OutputTransform declares (see OutputTransform)."""
+
+    before_reduce_scatter: bool = False
+
+    @classmethod
+    def of(cls, transform) -> Optional["TransformFacts"]:
+        if transform is None or isinstance(transform, cls):
+            return transform
+        return cls(before_reduce_scatter=transform.before_reduce_scatter)
+
+
+def facts_of(declaration):
+    """``declaration`` with its read, update and output transform reduced to
+    the capabilities they declare, and without the declarations it was
+    chained to. None stays None."""

+        return None
+    from dataclasses import replace
+
+    return replace(
+        declaration,
+        read=ReadFacts.of(declaration.read),
+        update=UpdateFacts.of(declaration.update),
+        output_transform=TransformFacts.of(declaration.output_transform),
+        previous=None,
+        prepared_from=None,
+    )
